title: Cinnamon Honey Butter
tagline: The Texas Roadhouse butter. Illegal to serve rolls without it.
description: The whipped cinnamon honey butter that makes the steakhouse rolls a pilgrimage: butter, honey, powdered sugar, cinnamon, whipped until it spreads like frosting. Two minutes of work, permanent household demand.
ingredients: 225g (2 sticks) unsalted butter, fully softened (leave it out 2 hours - actually softened)
steps: Beat the softened butter with a hand mixer (or stand mixer, whisk attachment) for 1 minute until creamy.
Add honey, powdered sugar, cinnamon, and salt. Beat 2-3 more minutes, scraping down once, until pale, fluffy, and visibly whipped - it should hold soft peaks like frosting.
Serve at room temperature. Refrigerate leftovers up to 2 weeks; let it come back to room temp (or re-whip 30 seconds) before serving.
notes: The whip is the recipe. Stirred-together ingredients taste the same but spread like cold spackle - the airiness is the Roadhouse texture.
Salted butter works: drop the added salt.
Also correct on: pancakes, cornbread, sweet potatoes, toast, a spoon.
troubleshooting: Grainy → butter wasn't soft enough to emulsify; let it warm and re-whip.
Separated or greasy → over-whipped in a warm kitchen; chill 10 minutes and whip briefly.
Too sweet → that's the recipe; halve the powdered sugar next time and it's still right.
